title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Water Supply"

Water supply is built one component at a time. Hydropower direct use is complete and is what
`water_supply_gep` currently carries. A water-use calculation covering agriculture, industry and
municipal withdrawals is ported and reported beside it as separate columns. The price convention
recorded in `es_config.csv` is `resource rent (CWoN 2024)`, and the base year is 2019.

## Hydropower

### Quantity and price

The hydropower valuation has no separate quantity and price step. CWoN 2024 publishes a
capitalised hydropower wealth per country, and the annual rent that wealth implies is what the
account wants.

### Valuation

`annuity_factor` is the present value of one dollar a year over the CWoN horizon,

$$
A = \sum_{t=1}^{100} \frac{1}{(1+r)^t}, \qquad r = 0.04
$$

and `hydropower_rent_from_wealth` divides each country's `YR2019` wealth by it. Countries without
wealth stay NaN, because no data is not zero rent.

The method was identified by reverse-engineering against the drive's committed 2019 output, whose
script is not on the drive. It is exact across all 94 valued countries, with the ratio constant to
1e-10. The test suite asserts the annuity identity and the exact replication. An earlier
direct-use script on the drive, price times quantity from EIA and World Bank series dated November
2024, is superseded by this method and is not ported.

## Water use

### Quantity and price

Withdrawal volumes in cubic metres per sector come from the withdrawal table. The price is the
AQUASTAT SDG 6.4.1 water-use efficiency series in US dollars per cubic metre, one series per
sector.

### Valuation

`clean_aquastat_water_efficiency` is script 01 of the drive's R calculation. It keeps the US$/m3 rows of
the four SDG 6.4.1 series and pivots them wide by country and year.

`water_use_gep_by_country_year` is script 02. It applies three country renames onto the withdrawal
table's spellings, fills iso codes for the names its country map does not carry, drops the
regional aggregate rows, merges the two tables, restricts to the survey years, and multiplies
efficiency by withdrawal per sector to give `gep_water_agricultural`, `gep_water_industrial` and
`gep_water_municipal`.

`water_use_components_from_chain` takes the latest survey year per country and keys it to r250 by
exact country-name match, first on `iso3_r250_name` and then on `name_long`. A calculation country with
no match keeps an empty iso3, so a name drift is visible instead of dropped.

Both of the R calculation's own outputs replicate. The cleaned efficiency table matches bit-exactly. The
country-year GEP table matches to the anchor CSV's own 15-significant-digit rounding, maximum
relative difference 3e-15.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, scoped to the `water_supply` service:

- `water_supply_cwon_hydro_wealth_path`, the CWoN `hydro_wealth_cd` table, with a `_source_url`
  row for the World Bank reproducibility archive and a `_source_archive_member` row naming the
  file inside it.
- `water_use_efficiency_input_path`, the raw AQUASTAT export, with a `_source_url` row for the
  AQUASTAT data API.
- `water_use_withdrawal_path`, the withdrawal table.
- `water_use_agriculture_path` and `water_use_all_sector_path`, the drive's committed per-country
  tables, held as comparison anchors.

## Outputs

- `hydropower_rent.csv` from the `hydropower_rent` task.
- `aquastat_water_efficiency_cleaned.csv`, `water_use_gep_by_country_year.csv` and
  `water_use_components.csv` from the `water_use_components` task.
- `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` from `gep_calculation`, holding the r250 identifiers and
  attributes, `year`, `hydropower_gep`, `water_use_agriculture_gep`,
  `water_use_all_sector_gep` and `water_supply_gep`.

## Method constants

- `water_supply_hydropower_capitalization_rate = 0.04` in `es_parameters`, the rate CWoN
  capitalized their wealth figure with.

  ⚠ **This is not the account's discount rate and must not be harmonized onto it.** The account
  discounts future benefits at 2 percent, with sensitivity at 1 and 3. This rate is doing the
  opposite job: CWoN published a *capitalized* wealth figure, and hydropower GEP is the annual
  rent inside it, so the module runs their capitalization backwards. Inverting with any rate but
  the one they capitalized with returns a rent CWoN never capitalized — the number would become
  wrong in the act of making it look consistent. The two quantities share a word and nothing else.
  The consistency gate knows the difference and reports both.
- `HYDROPOWER_HORIZON_YEARS = 100`, the CWoN capitalisation horizon.
- `HYDROPOWER_GEP_YEAR = 2019`, the wealth column the rent is read from. Current USD equals real
  2019 USD in the 2019 base year, and this is the only variant that covers Venezuela.
- `HYDROPOWER_REFERENCE_EXCLUDED`, seventeen iso3 codes set to NaN to reproduce the reference:
  AZE, BGR, DOM, GRC, GTM, HTI, KAZ, LBR, MAR, MKD, NIC, POL, PRT, SLV, TJK, UKR and ZAF.
- `WATER_USE_YEARS = (2000, 2005, 2010, 2015)`, the AQUASTAT survey years the calculation keeps.
- `WATER_USE_EFFICIENCY_SERIES`, `WATER_USE_COUNTRY_RENAMES`, `WATER_USE_ISO_LOOKUP` and
  `WATER_USE_REGIONS_DROPPED`, which reproduce script 02's name surgery verbatim.

## Taken as given

CWoN's own hydropower wealth estimate, and the AQUASTAT efficiency and withdrawal series.

## What is open

The seventeen excluded countries are the largest open item. The reference output leaves them empty
although the CWoN wealth table values them, and no available material explains the drop, because
the 2026 script is not on the drive and the package lacks its raw workbook. The exclusion is
encoded to reproduce the reference, the reason is an ask on the deck, and changing the list is a
reviewed-commit decision.

The drive's per-country water-use tables are not this calculation's outputs and are held as anchors
rather than adopted. The agriculture table equals 1000 times `GEP_total` from a separate crop-water
valuation whose scripts are not on the drive. The all-sector table was computed on a newer AQUASTAT
vintage with the appendix's deflate-to-2015 step, and only 3 of 183 countries reproduce from the
staged inputs, with a median committed to computed-at-2019 ratio of 0.36 over a range of 0 to 1.25.

Script 02's lookup countries keep their AQUASTAT names, so their efficiency and withdrawal rows
share an iso code but never a country name. The merge leaves them as half-rows with no products,
including USA, RUS and TUR. The anchor commits that behaviour and the port reproduces it.

`water_supply_gep` stays the hydropower component alone. How, and whether, the water-use components
combine with it is the account's subgroup question, flagged on the deck. The agriculture and
household components named on the group's sheet are not yet built anywhere we have seen, and the
module is laid out to receive them beside hydropower.
